source_text: Πεπλήρωται δὲ ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται τῶν παραπλησίων παραδόξων τῷ ἀναγραφέντι περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ παρὰ τῷ βαπτίσματι περὶ τῆς περιστερᾶς καὶ τῆς ἐξ οὐρανοῦ φωνῆς. σημεῖον δὲ οἶμαι τοῦ τότε ὀφθέντος ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐν εἴδει περιστερᾶς τὰ ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ παράδοξα γεγενημένα, ἅτινα διαβάλλων Κέλσος φησὶν αὐτὸν παρ᾿ Αἰγυπτίοις μεμαθηκότα πεποιηκέναι. καὶ οὐκ ἐκείνοις γε μόνοις χρήσομαι ἀλλὰ γὰρ κατὰ τὸ εἰκὸς καὶ οἷς οἱ ἀπόστολοι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ πεποιήκασιν. οὐκ ἂν γὰρ χωρὶς δυνάμεων καὶ παραδόξων ἐκίνουν τοὺς καινῶν λόγων καὶ καινῶν μαθημάτων ἀκούοντας πρὸς τὸ καταλιπεῖν μὲν τὰ πάτρια παραδέξασθαι δὲ μετὰ κινδύνων τῶν μέχρι θανάτου τὰ τούτων μαθήματα. καὶ ἔτι ἴχνη τοῦ ἁγίου ἐκείνου πνεύματος, ὀφθέντος ἐν εἴδει περιστερᾶς, παρὰ Χριστιανοῖς σῴζεται. ἐξεπᾴδουσι δαίμονας καὶ πολλὰς ἰάσεις ἐπιτελοῦσι καὶ ὁρῶσί τινα κατὰ τὸ βούλημα τοῦ λόγου περὶ μελλόντων. κἂν χλευάσῃ δὲ Κέλσος τὸ λεχθησόμενον ἢ ὃν εἰσήγαγεν Ἰουδαῖον, ὅμως λελέξεται ὅτι πολλοὶ ὡσπερεὶ ἄκοντες προσεληλύθασι χριστιανισμῷ, πνεύματός τινος τρέψαντος αὐτῶν τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν αἰφνίδιον ἀπὸ τοῦ μισεῖν τὸν λόγον ἐπὶ τὸ ὑπεραποθανεῖν αὐτοῦ καὶ φαντασιώσαντος αὐτοὺς ὕπαρ ἢ ὄναρ. πολλὰ γὰρ καὶ τοιαῦτα ἱστορήσαμεν· ἅτινα ἐὰν γράφωμεν αὐτοὶ αὐτοῖς παρατυχόντες καὶ ἰδόντες. γέλωτα πλατὺν ὀφλήσομεν τοῖς ἀπίστοις, οἰομένοις ἡμᾶς ὁμοίως οἷς ὑπολαμβάνουσι ταῦτ᾿ ἀναπεπλακέναι καὶ αὐτοὺς πλάσσειν. ἀλλὰ γὰρ θεὸς μάρτυς τοῦ ἡμετέρου συνειδότος, βουλομένου οὐ διὰ ψευδῶν ἀπαγγελιῶν ἀλλὰ διά τινος ἐναργείας ποικίλης συνιστάνειν τὴν Ἰησοῦ θείαν διδασκαλίαν. ἐπεὶ δὲ Ἰουδαῖός ἐστιν ὁ περὶ τοῦ ἀναγεγραμμένου ἁγίου πνεύματος κατεληλυθέναι ἐν εἴδει περιστερᾶς πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπορῶν, λεκτέον ἂν εἴη πρὸς αὐτόν· ὦ οὗτος, τίς ἐστιν ὁ ἐν τῷ Ἡσαΐᾳ λέγων· „καὶ νῦν κύριος ἀπέστειλέ με καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ;“ ἐν ῳ ἀμφιβόλου ὄντος τοῦ ῥητοῦ, πότερον ὁ πατὴρ καὶ τὸ ἄγιον πνεῦμα ἀπέστειλαν τὸν Ἰησοῦν, ἢ ὁ πατὴρ ἀπέστειλε τόν τε Χριστὸν καὶ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, τὸ δεύτερόν ἐστιν ἀληθές. καὶ ἐπεὶ ἀπεστάλη ὁ σωτὴρ, εἶτα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ εἰρημένον ὑπὸ τοῦ προφήτου, ἐχρῆν δὲ τὴν τῆς προφητείας πλήρωσιν ἐγνῶσθαι καὶ τοῖς ἑξῆς· διὰ τοῦτο ἀνέγραψαν οἱ Ἰησοῦ μαθηταὶ τὸ γεγενημένον.
pass_a_gloss: The law and prophets have been fulfilled of the similar paradoxes to the written thing about Jesus by the baptism about the dove and the voice from heaven. And I think a sign of the then appeared Holy Spirit in the form of a dove the paradoxes having been done by Jesus, which things accusing Celsus says he having learned from Egyptians did. And I will not use only these but also according to what is likely and what the apostles of Jesus have done. For they would not have moved the hearers of new words and new teachings to leave the paternal things and receive theirs with dangers up to death without powers and paradoxes. And still traces of that Holy Spirit appeared in the form of a dove are preserved among Christians. They cast out demons and perform many healings and see some things according to the will of the Word about things to come. And even if Celsus mocks what will be said or the Jew he introduced, nevertheless it will be said that many as if unwilling have come to Christianity, some spirit having turned their ruling part suddenly from hating the Word to dying for it and having imagined them to be above or in a dream. For we have narrated many such things, which things if we write having encountered and seen them ourselves. We will incur broad ridicule from the unbelievers thinking us to be like those they suppose these things to be fabricated and themselves to fabricate. But God is witness of our conscience willing not through false reports but through some varied manifestation to establish the divine teaching of Jesus. And since the Jew is in doubt about the written Holy Spirit having come in the form of a dove to Jesus, it should be said to him: O man, who is the one saying in Isaiah: 'And now the Lord has sent me and his Spirit?' In which it is ambiguous what is being said, whether the Father and the Holy Spirit sent Jesus or the Father sent both Christ and the Holy Spirit, the latter is true. And since the Savior was sent, then the Holy Spirit, so that what was said by the prophet might be fulfilled, but the fulfillment of the prophecy should have been known also to those who follow, for this reason the disciples of Jesus wrote what happened.

pass_b_english: The law and the prophets have been fulfilled through paradoxes like those recorded about Jesus at his baptism — the dove and the voice from heaven. I take this as a sign of the Holy Spirit who appeared then in the form of a dove, pointing to the extraordinary things Jesus did. Celsus accuses him of learning these from Egyptians and performing them, but I will not rely on these accounts alone. It is also probable, given what Jesus' apostles accomplished, that they could not have moved people hearing new words and new teachings to abandon their ancestral traditions and accept theirs — risking dangers even to death — unless they had been backed by powers and extraordinary events. Traces of that same Holy Spirit, who appeared as a dove, are still preserved among Christians: they cast out demons, perform many healings, and perceive certain future things according to the will of the Word. Even if Celsus mocks what I am about to say, or the Jewish interlocutor he introduces, it must still be said that many have come to Christianity as if against their will, some spirit suddenly turning their governing faculty from hating the Word to dying for it, and making them think they were in a trance or a dream. We have recorded many such cases; if we wrote them down after encountering and seeing them ourselves, we would only invite broad ridicule from unbelievers, who already suppose we fabricate these things just as they imagine. But God is witness to our conscience: we want to establish the divine teaching of Jesus not through false reports, but through some varied and clear manifestation. Since the Jew expresses doubt about the written account of the Holy Spirit descending in the form of a dove upon Jesus, one should say to him: 'Tell me, who is speaking in Isaiah when it says, "And now the Lord has sent me and his Spirit"?' (Isaiah 48:16). The passage is ambiguous — whether the Father and the Holy Spirit sent Jesus, or the Father sent both the Christ and the Holy Spirit. The second reading is the true one. And since the Savior was sent first, then the Holy Spirit, so that the prophet's words might be fulfilled, the fulfillment of that prophecy had to be made known to later generations as well. For this reason, Jesus' disciples recorded what took place.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A provides a literal gloss, and Pass B provides a fluent translation that preserves all nuances, including the distinction between the two interpretations of the Isaiah passage. The scripture citation (Isaiah 48:16) in Pass B correctly identifies the verse alluded to in the Greek (καὶ νῦν κύριος ἀπέστειλέ με καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ).
